media.altText:
❯ /mattpocock-skills:ask-matt After creating tickets, should i create a new session for implelenting ?

Yes — per the main flow's "Context hygiene" section: after /to-tickets, you /clear and start a fresh session per ticket, running /implement against that ticket's number.

The reasoning: the grilling → spec → tickets chain needs to stay in one unbroken context window so it all builds on the same thinking (which is exactly what we just did through this conversation). But once tickets are published with their blocking edges recorded on the tracker, each ticket is meant to be self-contained — /implement only needs the ticket body, CONTEXT.md, and the relevant ADRs, all of which now live on disk/tracker rather than in this conversation's memory. Carrying this whole conversation's context into implementation would just be dead weight.

Concretely for this repo: open a new session, and run /implement against issue #2 (the only one currently unblocked). Clear again for #3 etc.

Quick tip when using /to-tickets:

1. Think about how big the task is
2. Approximate how many tokens you'd need to spend to complete it (this takes experience - higher estimates are safer)
3. Divide that total by 150k (the approx smart zone of SOTA agents)
4. That gives you the number of tickets you need.

A big refactor might be 1M tokens. That's 6.66 smart zones, so 7 tickets.

Nice heuristic if you're not sure.

Agents exhibit a classic "bad developer" trait when debugging

They start to get hopeful. They say "we're getting closer". "This is the decisive piece of information".

This narrative builds until they say something like "we've eliminated all possible hypotheses". Or "this is the definitive fix".

Pull back. Don't jump to conclusions. Soft eyes.

I said "don't jump to conclusions yet". 2 turns later, the bug was solved.

I saw @dexhorthy interviewed by @GergelyOrosz recently - great chat, worth checking out

He talked about how AI coding sessions have a "trajectory"

I.e. the agent tends to pick up habits during the session. If it verifies the app by cURL once, it'll probably do it when you request the next change.

Sometimes you need to clear the context just to change trajectory.

I've even seen this when you have state that's retained across sessions. I've got a personal podcast generated from my feed. All previous podcast transcripts are available for it to view. So it picks up recurring catchphrases, and annoying traits. It's started over-focusing on meaningless metrics (wow, 400 bookmarks on this post!). My podcast is on a bad trajectory.

The "trajectory" metaphor gets really scary for codebases. Codebases are stateful - they accumulate state over sessions. So every codebase has a trajectory, and most trend down.

The only way to fix a bad trajectory is with better steering, and by changing the environment the agent works in.

Cool stuff. Thanks Dex
